summary: A list of RFCs by number as of June 1, 1971, giving the first author, title, date and NIC number for each document from RFC 1 onward. It is a reference tool for finding early memos. It was replaced by RFC 200.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 170 lists RFCs by number and gives each entry's author, title, date, and NIC number. It provides a more detailed index of early ARPANET documents.

questions: where is a list of early rfcs
what was the rfc list by number
subtitle: A 1971 RFC index adds authors, dates, titles, and NIC numbers to the list.

tldr.problem: Readers of the growing RFC collection needed an index with more detail than a brief list of titles and numbers.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 170 lists the first author, title, date, NIC number, and RFC number for each entry in its table.
tldr.outcome: The June 1971 list was later obsoleted by RFC 200, according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 170 is historic and was obsoleted by RFC 200. It preserves an index of early RFCs as of June 1, 1971.

sections.title: A More Detailed RFC Index
sections.content: RFC 170 is an RFC List by Number dated June 1, 1971. Its table includes the first author, title, date, NIC number, and RFC number for entries in the list. It is an index, not a protocol specification.
sections.plainLanguage: This index tells readers who wrote each RFC, what it was called, when it was dated, and which NIC number identified it.

sections.title: The Entries and Number Gaps
sections.content: The table includes entries starting with RFC 1 and continuing through RFC 170. It records some numbers as never issued and includes an entry for a revised RFC 137. The list therefore shows both documents and details about numbering in the series.
sections.plainLanguage: The list shows RFC entries and marks some numbers that had no RFC. It also notes a revision associated with RFC 137.

sections.title: A Snapshot of the Collection
sections.content: RFC 170 provides a dated view of the RFC list as of June 1, 1971. The unit metadata says RFC 200 later obsoleted it. The list's entries preserve the titles and publication information presented at that time.
sections.plainLanguage: This document captures what the RFC list looked like on its publication date. A later list replaced it.
